question: Check whether function $f(x)$ defined as $f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{|x-3|}{2(x-3)}, & x < 3 \\ \frac{x-6}{6}, & x \ge 3 \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x = 3$ or not.
explanation:
**Step 1: Find the Left-Hand Limit (LHL)**  
For $x < 3$, $|x-3| = -(x-3)$. So,  
$$\lim_{x \to 3^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 3^-} \frac{-(x-3)}{2(x-3)} = \lim_{x \to 3^-} -\frac{1}{2} = -\frac{1}{2}$$

**Step 2: Find the Right-Hand Limit (RHL)**  
For $x \ge 3$, $f(x) = \frac{x-6}{6}$. So,  
$$\lim_{x \to 3^+} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 3^+} \frac{x-6}{6} = \frac{3-6}{6} = -\frac{3}{6} = -\frac{1}{2}$$

**Step 3: Find the Function Value at $x = 3$**  
Since $x = 3$ belongs to the second branch ($x \ge 3$):  
$$f(3) = \frac{3-6}{6} = -\frac{1}{2}$$  
Since LHL = RHL = $f(3) = -\frac{1}{2}$, the function is continuous at $x = 3$.
